text:
Night on the water.

I told you so,

night on the water.


Four stars

nail the air,

four stars.

The night is worth

four skies.


The river carries away

time and jewel,

night on the water.


Night carrying its enormous sky;

where it trembles over its breasts

it shines in the river

with the fall of some star.


A star fell.

All night I leaned my elbows

on illuminated railings.


The breeze spread its forget-me-nots,

and the sweet vapor

sways the air the wind steals

as it steals

hummingbirds without a hand.


Night that reckons

the clear accounts of its stars

on papers the river wets.

Through the willow groves

passed the wave that knows figures

and miscounts the stars that rise late.


With what gaze

do I seek the night that is lost to me

beyond the harvest

of stars

and shines hidden at black backs.


Night on the shore of my presence

that dissolves me into sweetgum.


Time that lets loose

and then binds.


The air shines: time and jewel.


To the corners of fireflies

the night descends.


And there is an X-ray hand

that enters my eyes and takes them away

to hide another gaze from them.

Night on the water.


I told you:

night on the water.

translation.title: Night on the Water
translation.editorial_note: The refrain, short stanzas, forget-me-not image, and river-and-starlight imagery are preserved.
